Tonight through Tuesday: A broad low near Redmond, Oregon 
Sunday afternoon, migrates to the southern Panhandle of Idaho 
early Monday and Montana by Monday afternoon. At the same time a
secondary upper low on its heels is drawn over the Cascades 
Monday before that too shifts into western Montana by Tuesday 
morning. A deformation axis/boundary sits around the eastern CWA
and the southerly flow ahead of the main low will continue 
drawing on PWAT fetch (140-160% of normal). 

For this afternoon and tonight the lift with the low, the 
moisture and an area of 400-900 J/kg of MUCAPE over eastern WA 
and ID will lead to increasing rain showers and a chance for 
thunderstorms. The best chances from this development will be 
over southeast WA/lower ID and could expand somewhat rapidly 
north through the late afternoon to evening. Locally heavy rain,
gusty winds and lightning will be possible. Farther west a 
chance for showers will linger over the Cascades and central WA,
with the better chances pushing back against the Cascades and 
north-central WA.

Then heading into Monday the lingering deformation axis and 
secondary low coming on the heels of the first will keep rain 
showers going across the eastern third of WA and Idaho with PoPs
around 50-90%. The highest chances will be around Idaho. Other 
chances will re-emerge near the Cascades and central WA through 
the afternoon and evening Monday too, but PoPs will remain 
around 20-30% there. Heading into Monday evening into overnight 
the secondary low migrates east and starts to draw the higher 
PoPs closer to the ID/MT border, but the proximity of the low 
and modest moisture with will keep chances going into Tuesday 
morning. Then by Tuesday afternoon the risk for showers retreats
to north Idaho.

The WPC continues to have a marginal excessive rainfall threat 
for the far eastern reaches of WA and all of ID today and 
tonight and mainly Idaho Monday, where steadier rain may allow 
some modest rain amounts. This will bring a risk for burn scar 
debris flows, rock slides and some rises on small creeks and 
streams. Rain amounts around the eastern third of WA and ID are 
forecast to range between 0.10 to 0.30 inches and around 0.25 
to 0.75 inches across Idaho, with locally over 1 inch possible 
around the some of the higher terrain across the north and 
central ID Panhandle mountains. Meanwhile, central WA and the 
Cascades could see trace amounts to 0.05 inches. Any 
thunderstorms could produce locally higher rain amounts.

Winds will increase some Monday. West winds of 10-15 mph with 
gusts of 15 to 25 mph will be possible, especially the Upper 
Columbia Basin, Palouse and the Spokane/CdA area. Highs Monday 
will be in the upper 50s and 60s over the east third of WA and 
ID, while central WA will see upper 60s and 70s. Tuesday will 
see upper 60s and 70s. Lows will be in the 40s to low 50s.

Wednesday to Sunday: The middle part of the work week turns 
drier and warm, before the next low approaches toward the later 
part of the week and weekend. Guidance starts to differ in the 
evolution of that low but the general trend is there. Wednesday
and Thursday remain dry, but winds are forecast to increase 
Thursday out of the west. Right now models support 10-20 mph 
winds with gusts of 20-25 mph locally near 30-35 mph around the 
Waterville Plateau. Highs will be in the 70s and 80s, with a few
areas possibly approaching 90 in the deeper basin. Region RH 
values drop some, though they generally remain above critical 
values. Still if the forecast holds there could be some locally 
elevated fire weather conditions Thursday. 

Then Thursday night into Sunday the low moves into area, 
increasing shower chances around the region. There could be some
embedded t-storms, but the risk is too low to include in the 
official forecast. Locally breezy conditions are possible around
central WA and the Cascades gaps. Highs are forecast to be in 
the upper 60s and 70s, with lows in the 40s to low 50s and 
locally some upper 30s in the sheltered valleys on the weekend. 
/Solveig
